model: Cleaver-Brooks Falcon (Honeywell SOLA-based) boiler control via BASgatewayLX
applies_to: Cleaver-Brooks Falcon hydronic boiler controls on Modbus, read by a BASgatewayLX.
summary: Gateway profile for the Cleaver-Brooks Falcon: 816 objects (121 AI, 440 AO, 115 BI, 140 BO), but only 7 are polled by default (firing rate, fan speed, flame signal, burner run time and three pump outputs). The rest of the Falcon register map is in it: status-change flags, burner control state and lockout code, CH/DHW demand and setpoints, pump status, limits and hundreds of configuration parameters as outputs.
notes: Built from Contemporary Controls' BASgatewayLX Modbus device profile CleaverBrooks_Falcon_b_LX.csv; the profile maps the registers in the Falcon Modbus guide (750-308) (https://www.ccontrols.com/support/dp/750-308FalconModbus.pdf).
Object instances are the ones this profile assigns when it is loaded into the gateway. A site that edited or rebuilt the profile may use different instances.
Only 7 of the 816 rows are flagged for polling in the profile; the rest are served only after you tick them in the gateway. Their descriptions say "not polled by default".

The CSV has no read/write column: Analog/Binary Inputs are read-only and Analog/Binary Outputs are commandable (priority array), which is how the gateway maps them (access inferred). Descriptions give the Modbus register each object reads.
Some names appear more than once in the profile as published (CH setpoint source; DHW storage time; CH pump overrun time...); they are kept as printed and told apart by instance.

integration.summary: Enable the burner control state, lockout code, outlet temperature and CH setpoint objects before mapping, then write the CH setpoint if the BMS sets it.
setup: The BASgatewayLX presents each Modbus device as its own virtual BACnet device on BACnet IP; give it a unique device instance and Modbus address (serial) or IP address (Modbus TCP) when you add it with this profile.
One BASgatewayLX handles up to 100 Modbus devices and 1000 polled points in total, so leave unneeded rows unpolled.
gotchas: Most configuration outputs (passwords, rates, limits) live in non-volatile memory; don't write them cyclically.
Unpolled rows do not appear as BACnet objects until enabled in the gateway's device profile page.
